t.E380.agn: In 1979 JECFA evaluated triammonium citrate within the 'not limited' ADI set for citric acid and its salts. No separate toxicological monograph was prepared for this substance.
t.E380.body: Citrate is a normal intermediate of the tricarboxylic acid (Krebs) cycle, which produces energy in the body. Ammonium enters the body's nitrogen metabolism; it is used to make substances such as glutamine, and the end product of this metabolism is urea.
t.E380.found.0: May be used in many foods in the EU at quantum satis (as much as needed)
t.E380.prod: Obtained by neutralising citric acid with ammonia.
t.E380.regx.0: ADI 'not limited'; included in the ADI for citric acid and its salts.
t.E380.regx.1: Group I additive; generally permitted at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E380.summary: The ammonium salt of citric acid. Used as an acidity regulator.
t.E380.what: The ammonium salt of citric acid; a substance that buffers (balances) acidity.
